gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Creality's '10 mm basswood in one pass' rating for the Falcon A1 Pro 20W did not hold up in CNX Software's test (7 passes at 85% power and still not fully cut through), or that xTool's M2 FAQ ties its own cut ratings to 100% power and gives the 10W 3 mm black-acrylic cut as a 2-pass job.
standout_why: Compared against maker-wise.com (cited in chat 1). It already explains optical vs electrical watts and notes Ortur and Creality quote optical output, so that common normalisation is taken. But it repeats 'Creality rates the A1 Pro at 10 mm basswood in one pass' as an untested maker claim and says it didn't test the machines. It gives no pass counts or speeds behind any depth figure. I couldn't check the two other pages: WebFetch got only the title for Tom's Hardware best-picks (cited in both chats) and for the xTool beginner guide (cited in chat 1), so I can't rule out that they hold pass-count data. Neither ChatGPT answer gives any cut depth with conditions. Chat 2 calls the A1 Pro 'better for frequent wood cutting' on the strength of its 20 W rating alone.
decides: This confirms rather than overturns the pick. A beginner can't upgrade to the A1 Pro (from $1,099 on Creality's US store) expecting one-pass thick cuts: CNX Software's 10 mm basswood cut took 7 passes and still had to be separated by hand. Put side by side under the makers' own conditions, the M2 10W's cut ratings (100% power, single pass) cover the 3 mm stock beginners mostly use. That supports keeping the xTool M2 10W ($499 on xTool's store) as the beginner pick. Pitch 20 W as faster on thin stock (xTool's FAQ: 3 mm basswood at 15 mm/s vs 8 mm/s), not as a way to cut thick wood in one pass. The footnote: maker cut depths are best-case one-pass ratings, and the one independent thick-cut test needed 7 passes.
